title: chsql.CounterDelta's reset-detection comparison is neutered so it never fires
notes: Real production seam, not a textual stand-in: chsql.CounterDelta (internal/chsql/builder.go, the typed compound-idiom behind counterDeltaFrag in internal/chsql/range_window.go ~2690-2707) renders `arrayMap((p, c) -> if(c < p, c, c - p), ...)` -- the counter-reset-aware pairwise delta rate()/increase() reduce over. The patch changes the comparison's second operand from `p` to `c` (`Lt(BareIdent("c"), BareIdent("p"))` -> `Lt(BareIdent("c"), BareIdent("c"))`), which is always false, so the emitted SQL always takes the `c - p` branch and the reset-compensation arm never fires: this is a disable, not merely an inversion. gen.CounterResetCase (test/property/gen/counter_reset.go) seeds a genuine mid-window reset (20 -> 5 between adjacent samples, not a duplicate timestamp -- see that file's header on why test/property/rate_dup_timestamp_test.go's duplicate-timestamp dataset does not exercise this). Locally reproduced end to end: the unmutated code returns the Prometheus-correct increase() = 33.333... (100/3); with this patch applied to a scratch copy the same query returns 6.666... (20/3, i.e. last-first with no reset added back), and TestPromQL_CounterResetMidWindowCompensation fails with exactly that drift. TestPromQL_RangeWindowBoundaryExactSample (the sibling MUTANT-PROMQL-RANGE-WINDOW-BOUNDARY-CLOSED-LEFT's own detector) was re-run against this same patch and still passes, confirming the two mutants are independently attributable.
